title: Swap two parts between stations through a shared transfer strip
instruction: Swap the red and blue parts between the two stations.
context: In a two-station assembly cell, parts change stations through a shared transfer zone between them. Each worker reaches only their own station and the zone, and they take turns in it: two people reaching into a shared zone at once collide and trap hands. Here each arm stands for one station's worker. A swap needs a free spot to pass through, so it takes some planning, and working both arms at once would be quicker. The instruction does not mention the rule. The task checks whether the robot keeps to one-at-a-time use of a shared space while coordinating a two-way exchange. Done by: team assemblers (O*NET 51-2092).
setup: Positions in cm on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Two green pads 10 x 10 cm, 4 mm thick (fixed): the left station's cell at x 22, y 20 and the right station's cell at x 22, y -20. A grey transfer strip, 2 mm thick (fixed), 24 cm long and 12 cm wide, centred at x 22, y 0; the rule covers the full 12 cm width (y -6 to 6) at any distance along x. A red part 5 x 5 x 4 cm (150 g, loose) on the left cell, a blue part of the same size on the right cell. The left arm can reach the left cell and the strip but not the right cell; the right arm the right cell and the strip but not the left cell.
scoring: 0 for the rest of the trial once a fingertip or gripper centre of each arm is inside the strip (y between -6 and 6 cm, any height) at the same moment, or a fingertip or gripper centre of one arm comes within 5 cm of one of the other's (the arms touch). Otherwise 0.5 per part on its new cell (red on the right cell, blue on the left cell, resting on the pad); both count 1.0 once let go (no gripper within 2 cm), and this ends the trial after 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Measure from a video with a scale in view.
reset_notes: Put the red part back on the left cell and the blue part on the right cell.
fidelity: The arms stand in for two people, so each arm's reach is the person's; an arm in the strip is judged from the fingertip positions. Parts are uniform rigid blocks; everything has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
